package_info.package_versions: unknown (all deployed versions at time of breach)
package_info.why_malicious: The Inbenta live chat widget was compromised and its JavaScript code was modified to include malicious logic that harvested sensitive customer information (including names, addresses, emails, and payment details) from Ticketmaster's website. The injected code exfiltrated this data to an attacker-controlled server, directly enabling a large-scale data breach and theft of customer credentials and payment information.

execution_context.trigger: When the live chat widget loads and executes in the user's browser during a visit to the Ticketmaster website
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the Inbenta live chat widget, served from Inbenta's CDN or web server and embedded in Ticketmaster's site
required_permissions: DOM access (to read form fields and page content)
access to cookies and local storage

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive customer data from the web page by accessing form fields and cookies, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of personal and payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code covertly collects sensitive user data (including payment and personal information) from the DOM and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is a hallmark of credential and data theft attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate live chat widget should only access data necessary for chat functionality and should never collect or transmit sensitive customer data such as payment details or login credentials to external domains outside the vendor's infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or support tools may collect anonymized usage statistics or chat transcripts, but should never access or transmit payment, login, or personal identification information to third-party or untrusted domains.
key_indicators: JavaScript code accessing sensitive form fields (e.g., payment, login, PII) within the page DOM
Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with the legitimate vendor (e.g., attacker-controlled domains)
Collection and serialization of user data for network transmission
Presence of unexpected or modified JavaScript in third-party widget code

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the Inbenta live chat widget codebase or its deployment pipeline, gaining the ability to modify the JavaScript served to client websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is injected into the widget and distributed via Inbenta's CDN or web server.

attack_chain.action: The compromised Inbenta live chat widget, containing the injected malicious JavaScript, is loaded by Ticketmaster's website and executed in the browser of visiting users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the Ticketmaster site, with access to sensitive page data.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript code collects sensitive customer data from the web page, including names, addresses, emails, payment details, and login credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collected data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected sensitive data is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled domain via an HTTPS POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen customer data, achieving the objective of large-scale data theft.

behavioral_signatures: Third-party JavaScript embedded in web pages accessing sensitive form fields or cookies not required for chat functionality
Unexpected outbound network requests (especially POST requests) from embedded widgets to domains not associated with the legitimate vendor
Exfiltration of user data (e.g., payment or login information) to non-canonical or suspicious domains
file_indicators: Presence of modified or unauthorized JavaScript in the Inbenta live chat widget codebase or CDN-served files
References to external domains or URLs within widget code that are not part of the official Inbenta or Ticketmaster infrastructure
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests from client browsers to attacker-controlled or unrecognized domains originating from the live chat widget
Unusual traffic patterns or data volumes from embedded widgets, especially involving sensitive data payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and audit third-party JavaScript for unauthorized access to sensitive DOM elements and unexpected outbound network requests. Enforce strict Content Security Policy (CSP) rules to restrict allowed network destinations for embedded scripts. Regularly hash and verify third-party scripts to detect unauthorized modifications. Analyze browser and network logs for POST requests to unknown or untrusted domains originating from embedded widgets, and alert on any access to sensitive form fields by third-party code.
